messages:
Dana: noticed a spike in PCIe link resets and Xid 13 errors across multiple racks starting ~02:07 UTC, capacity drop ~18% in us-west2.
ops-bot: ALERT: gpu.pcie.reset.rate threshold breached on us-west2
Kevin: can you confirm it's not soft-ECC? what's the Xid code?
Dana: tails from node rack-22-host07:
```
[02:06:45] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:5c:00): 13, PID 21104: GPF on enqueue
[02:06:46] kernel: PCIe link down/up, retry
[02:06:47] NVRM: GPU has fallen off the bus
[02:06:50] nvidia: driver reset requested
```
Dana: also motherboard logs show repeated PCI Bus Reset events.
Mira: pattern looks like link flaps. Any common BOM across affected hosts?
Dana: yes — all affected are board rev B3 with BMC/BIOS v2.4.0 we rolled last week. racks on B2 are fine.
Jonah: that matches canary failures we saw in a couple hosts but didn't escalate. did we see any correlation with power cycling?
Dana: some hosts exhibit pre-suspend power PM events right before the reset.
Mira: probable regression in power sequencing from the B3 firmware. vendor? we should open an urgent SR but avoid mass drain for now.
Tara: what's customer impact? latency or errors visible to users?
Dana: routed generation latency +11%, some 504s observed. autoscaler shifted tasks to eu-west1 to maintain SLOs.
Kevin: mitigation proposal: 1) tag B3 racks as no-new-alloc, 2) reduce GPU prefetch/p2p settings on B3 hosts, 3) step-drain only persistent offenders.
Mira: agree. and add placement policy to avoid routing critical traffic to B3.
Jonah: applying tag: `rbctl tag set rack-22 no-new-alloc` -> ok.
```
$ rbctl tag set rack-22 no-new-alloc
ok: rack-22 tagged
```
Dana: quick throttle script ran on three worst nodes, local error counts dropped.
```
for h in rack-22-host{07,08,09}; do ssh $h 'echo 8 > /sys/module/nvidia/parameters/max_concurrent_streams'; done
```
Kevin: vendor flagged B3 change affects PCIe power sequencing and NVLink negotiation. rollback to B2 not trivial; vendor investigating.
Tara: ops cost note: replacing hardware or wide drains would be ~$130k + lost capacity. software mitigations shift cost to cross-region egress and overprovision (~$18k this week).
Mira: open SR and add i2c, BMC, and kernel logs. Jonah, can you create the ticket?
Jonah: VSUP-4021 created, uploaded dmesg, i2c, and board serials: https://vendor.ticket/VSUP-4021/logs
ops-bot: TICKET CREATED: VSUP-4021 assigned to vendor-team
Mira: actions: vendor escalation (Jonah), placement tag (done), throttle/prefetch disable (Mira/Dana), step-drain when Xid > 10/hr (Kevin).
Dana: monitoring dashboard: peak errors 8.1 errors/min at 02:08 UTC, down to 1.4/min after mitigations.
Tara: good. keep me updated if we need customer notifications; prefer to hold until severity crosses threshold.
Kevin: add a rollout gate to firmware process to detect PCIe reset anomalies during canary.
Mira: filing RFC for rollout gate.
Dana: update 02:42 UTC: vendor requested per-host full i2c and BMC logs; Jonah uploaded. continuing to monitor.
Jonah: vendor replied: investigating power sequencing race in B3. will follow up with patch or guidance.
Dana: errors continue to sporadically flap on a subset of GPUs; holding drains and using placement + throttle. will post another update in 30m.
Tara: thanks all. :thumbsup:
